items.stem: What does a service control policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations do?

options.text: Sets the maximum available permissions for accounts/OUs
options.rationale: Correct: an SCP is a guardrail capping permissions; it does not grant them.

options.text: Grants IAM permissions to users directly
options.rationale: SCPs do not grant; IAM policies grant within the SCP boundary.
SCPs are permission boundaries, not encryption.

items.explanation: Correct: an SCP caps permissions as a guardrail.

items.stem: Which TWO AWS services provide detective governance evidence? (Select TWO.)

options.text: AWS CloudTrail for API activity logging
options.rationale: Correct: CloudTrail records API calls for audit.

options.text: AWS Config for resource configuration history and rules
options.rationale: Correct: Config tracks config state and compliance.
SES sends email; it is not a governance evidence service.
Polly is text-to-speech, unrelated to governance.

items.explanation: Correct: CloudTrail and Config provide detective evidence.

items.stem: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS compliance certifications cover:

options.rationale: Correct: AWS attests the infrastructure; the customer must still configure their workloads correctly.

options.text: All of the customer's own configurations automatically
options.rationale: Customer configuration is the customer's responsibility.
Customers own their application code and data.
AWS certifications do cover the infrastructure layer.

items.explanation: Correct: certifications cover security 'of' the cloud.
